newsitem.title: UK: British guards may be stripped of bear necessities.
newsitem.headline: British guards may be stripped of bear necessities.

text.p: Canada's brown bears may be spared the indignity of ending up on the heads of British soldiers after the government said on Wednesday it was reviewing the use of the traditional bearskin hat.
Animal-loving Defence Minister Lord Gilbert has told the army to look at synthetic alternatives to the present headgear, known as the busby, the Defence Ministry said.
But for regiments that wear the busby, fake fur could prove a disaster because previous experiments failed the fashion test when confronted with the British weather.
"When the hats are dry they attract a great deal of static electricity. It looks like a punk hairstyle. They stand up in little points," an army spokesman said.
"In the rain they look like a lady might look when she steps out of the shower. Synthetics don't imitate long-haired animal furs well."

Nearly 3,000 soldiers, including the red-clad footguards outside Buckingham Palace, from five regiments such as the Grenadier, Scots and Welsh Guards have worn busbies since the battle of Waterloo in 1815.
The raw material for the headgear, which has made the guards a major tourist attraction, comes from the Canadian brown bear and the fur is then dyed black.
The hats have the added advantage of longevity.
"They are nearly everlasting," the spokesman said, explaining that only the leather interior and chin-straps have to be replaced.
"Lord Gilbert has not suggested banning the use of bearskins, but has merely asked the army to provide the rationale for their use," the spokesman said.
The Canadian High Commission in London said the country's aboriginal peoples would view a possible ban on the bearskins with great sorrow.
"They would regard it as yet more pressure on their traditional lifestyles from societies which have less harmony with the living world than they have," a spokesman said.
